reading.body:
Wi-Fi Communication Aulla in Tuscany is tagged as a data center on OpenStreetMap but appears to be a wireless ISP equipment site, not a commercial colocation facility serving external customers.

The facility is located in Aulla, a small town in Lunigiana where mountainous terrain makes wired broadband infrastructure costly to deploy. A fixed-wireless ISP would operate a base station and network operations point here to serve regional customers over radio rather than fiber or copper lines. This represents real telecom infrastructure and a genuine data-handling operation, but at a different scale and business model than the hyperscaler and colocation data centers that directly support large-scale AI workloads.

The distinction matters for understanding infrastructure inventory. A wireless ISP's equipment site is not part of the data center supply chain for AI training or inference, though it does handle data traffic. The site's small size and rural purpose make it unsuitable for the power density and redundancy requirements of compute-intensive AI operations. OpenStreetMap's data-center tag appears to have captured this as infrastructure without distinguishing between facilities by function or scale.

Research on this facility is incomplete. No operator website or business registration was confirmed before search quotas were exhausted, leaving uncertainty about actual current use, power draw, and operator identity. The nearest airport is 8.4 miles away in Sarzana, providing geographic reference but no inference about data flows or connectivity.
